card.name: Qeej dance
card.era: Centuries-old; rooted in Hmong ancestral tradition
card.tagline: Hmong reed-organ dance that guides souls and dazzles crowds
card.profile: The qeej (pronounced 'keng') is the Hmong free-reed bamboo mouth-organ and the acrobatic dance performed while playing it; the player spins, leaps, crouches and somersaults without interrupting the melody (Organology; Grinnell College). At Hmong New Year it is competitive entertainment, but its sacred role is at funerals, where qeej speech-surrogate melodies encode poems instructing the soul of the deceased on its journey to the ancestral realm (Falk, Asian Folklore Studies 2004). Players dance in symbolically meaningful circular movements during ceremonies (Grinnell College).
card.insight: The qeej is the Hmong cognate of the Chinese lusheng and the Lao khaen; on English Wikipedia the instrument is covered under 'Lusheng', while German Wikipedia titles its article 'Qeej' (Wikidata Q1595537).
